title: Compatibility wrapper for vector search: pagination contract and HTTP status normalization
creator: Priya Desai
description:
Problem: Multiple customers and older SDKs depend on legacy embeddings/rerank semantics: offset-based cursors, inconsistent HTTP error mapping (some services return 402/403/500 variants), and different tokenization/normalization between vector producers. This causes client-side breakage after runtime/model upgrades and makes rollouts risky. Goal: implement a backward-compatible API compatibility wrapper that normalizes pagination semantics, unifies HTTP status mapping for common error classes, and performs light token/embedding canonicalization at the edge so new model variants can be rolled out without breaking legacy clients.

Scope: wrapper applies to /v1/embeddings, /v1/embeddings/rerank and the vector-search help endpoints used by internal SDKs. It must: 1) accept both legacy offset/limit query form and the modern opaque cursor; 2) return a normalized HTTP error schema and mapped status codes; 3) enforce a stable max_page_size and deterministic ordering; 4) optionally coerce embedding dimensionality when models differ by compatible shapes (with explicit telemetry). Not in scope: re-training models or changing canonical embedding representations in training pipelines.
acceptance_criteria: Wrapper accepts legacy pagination (page & per_page / offset & limit) and modern 'cursor' token interchangeably; successful responses include 'next_cursor' (opaque) when more results exist

HTTP error mapping table implemented and documented: legacy 4xx/5xx variants normalized into our contract (e.g., quota->429 with structured error body; backend overload->503 with retry-after where appropriate)
Edge canonicalizer emits metrics when embedding dimensionality is coerced and does not drop vectors; customers can opt out via header 'X-RI-Compatibility: none'
SDKs (python/js) test harnesses confirm no regressions across 3 legacy client versions and current trunk; smoke tests included in pipeline
Runbook created for incidents where wrapper mapping causes visible client-side failures and an automated rollback toggle is available in Console
rollout_plan: Phase 1: Feature-flagged rollout to 5% of traffic in staging (canary route by customer-tier); collect telemetry for pagination mismatch rates
Phase 2: Expand to 25% after 72h with no regression signals; enable explicit opt-out header for enterprise customers to test clients against new model variants
Phase 3: Full rollout with a 7-day guarded ramp and automated rollback on error spikes defined by SLA thresholds
test_plan: Unit tests for cursor compatibility: convert between offset+limit and opaque cursor and back, ensure deterministic ordering and idempotency
Integration tests that replay historical client traces through the wrapper and assert identical response shapes
Fault-injection: return a variety of legacy error statuses from downstream model service and assert mapped status and structured error body
End-to-end SDK tests (python/js) that run against the canary endpoint and validate retry semantics and cursor parsing
monitoring: Dashboards: per-route cursor-parse-failures, per-customer mapping count, alert on >1% client-visible schema regressions over 5m
SLOs: any mapped error that changes semantics must not increase client error-rate by >0.5% during rollout window
notes: Related PM threads: PM-31789 (pagination harmonization), PM-33100 (cursor canonicalization)
